title: The post office
description: Send a parcel and deal with the paper that goes with it.

explanation.summary: Sending something means a box, a weight, a stamp and a form. The perfect is the right tense for a parcel that is already on its way, because the story of that parcel is not finished yet.

sections.heading: The parcel
sections.body: El paquete needs an address, a weight and a stamp. At the counter you say: quiero enviar este paquete a Madrid, ¿cuánto cuesta el envío?, pesa dos kilos. El envío is what you pay for and what travels, el sello is the stamp you put on it, and the person who sends it is el remitente.

examples.es: Quiero enviar este paquete a Madrid.
examples.en: I want to send this parcel to Madrid.

examples.es: El paquete pesa dos kilos y medio.
examples.en: The parcel weighs two and a half kilos.

sections.heading: What you have already done
sections.body: When the parcel is already on its way, use the perfect: he enviado el paquete, he pagado el envío, he escrito la dirección. These say the job is done and something is still happening because of it. If you name a finished time, use the preterite instead: envié el paquete ayer, lo envié por la mañana.

examples.es: He enviado el paquete esta mañana.
examples.en: I have sent the parcel this morning.

sections.heading: The paper that travels
sections.body: A lot of the work of a post office is paper. El formulario is the form you fill in at the counter, la carta is a letter and el recibo is the slip of paper that proves you paid. El código postal goes in the corner of the envelope. If the parcel leaves the country, pasa por la aduana, and there is another form to fill in.

examples.es: Rellené el formulario y firmé el recibo.
examples.en: I filled in the form and signed the receipt.

examples.es: Escribe el código postal en la esquina.
examples.en: Write the postcode in the corner.
